newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds extend rally, but volumes low.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds extend rally, but volumes low.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds extended their end-of-year rally further on Tuesday, with the 10-year OLO outperforming Bunds but volumes remaining limited and activity largely professional, dealers said.
"The market's bullish but volume is quite low. People are reluctant to come in at these levels," said one dealer, adding that the prospect of capital gains tax was keeping sellers away.
The 2006 OLO yield stood at 5.72 percent by 1540 GMT, its premium over Bunds narrowing to 11 basis points from 13 bps at the previous close and after edging out to 14 early in the session.

Bonds suffered no negative effect from news the European Commission had decided the Belgian government must reclaim 11.4 billion Belgian francs of illegal state aid it paid to exporting companies under its "Maribel" schemes.
December bond futures ended up 26 basis points at 122.22 after hitting a fresh contract high of 122.37.
Some dealers said a downward correction due to profittaking was likely once the new year arrived.
But others saw no immediate reason for a fall, saying U.S. data showed little reason right now to fear a U.S. rate rise while speculation had been revived of further cuts in German rates.
